newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris court jails Moslem militants.
newsitem.headline: Paris court jails Moslem militants.

text.p: A Paris court on Thursday jailed members of an alleged militant Moslem support network for up to eight years on charges of ordering attacks in Morocco, including one in which two Spaniards died in 1994.
Abdelilah Ziyad, a 38-year-old Moroccan who admitted setting up the network to undermine King Hassan II, was sent down for eight years.
A second Moroccan ringleader, Mohamed Zinedine, 36, was given a eight-year sentence in his absence.
Djamel Lounici, a 34-year-old Algerian Moslem fundamentalist currently being held in Italy, was sentenced to five years.

Prosecutors had requested jail terms of up to 10 years for the 34 accused, 13 of whom were being tried in absentia. The accused are believed to have been recruited by the ringleaders between 1988 and 1994 in the Paris area, Orleans and the eastern town of Besancon.
Police said the network was dismantled after four guerrilla attacks in Morocco in 1994 including the shooting of the Spanish tourists during a robbery at a Marrakesh hotel.
A Moroccan court has sentenced three people to death over the attack, including two French youths of North African origin.
The other attacks failed. They targetted Jews in Casablanca, police in Fes and nude bathers in Tangiers.
The trial opened in December days after a rush-hour bomb attack on a Paris commuter train killed four people, spurring fears of revenge attacks on France by fundamentalist guerrillas.
